event.title: SF AI Research Hack
event.summary: Our hypothesis is that existing AI scientist swarms get stuck because they are bored, trapped in repetitive, low-payoff loops long after returns have diminished. Artificial Scientist Swarms adds a deterministic Boredom Meter grounded in psychology so the swarm does not stay bored. Recomputed from the shared experiment ledger, it tracks stagnation, novelty deficit and overload to detect boredom and force a seeking state, moving from routine exploitation to paradigm breakout. We test this controller on known benchmarks and an Ig Nobel challenge: research that makes you laugh, then think. Agents search via Exa, share memory on past.dev, pre-register real-data tests, and can be ranked by a two-judge committee and final IgJudge. The controller is implemented; the published comparisons do not establish a statistically significant improvement.

boredom.title: Why a boredom meter?
paragraphs: In psychology, boredom is not laziness. It is the signal that a routine has stopped paying off and that it is time to look for something new (Westgate & Wilson 2018; Eastwood et al. 2012; Bench & Lench 2013).

Caffeinated turns that signal into a measured quantity B between 0 and 1 that steers the swarm. B is high when recent attempts mean the same thing as earlier ones, when nothing has significantly improved for a while, and when attempts keep failing or repeating.

It is never an LLM opinion: B is a deterministic function of the experiment ledger, so any agent can recompute any other agent's boredom and check it. It combines novelty, stagnation and overload (B = 0.45·(1 − novelty) + 0.45·stagnation + 0.10·overload).
